title: Vita3K designs cloud saves around visible local and remote state
summary: The V3KN storage manager compares timestamps and sizes, confirms overwrites, reports progress, and connects per-title upload or download to authenticated user sessions.
heroAlt: Source evidence from Vita3K pull request #3805: gui: Add Vita3K Network (V3KN) cloud save manager

sourceLabels.vita3k-pr-3805: gui: Add Vita3K Network (V3KN) cloud save manager

blocks.text: Cloud saves need conflict information before a copy button

A useful save manager must identify the signed-in user, discover which title is selected, inspect local and remote copies, show timestamp and total size, and explain which side will be overwritten. Simply uploading a directory in the background can destroy a newer playthrough. It must also package the multi-file savedata tree consistently and recover when the network disappears during a transfer.
Online storage becomes a first-class emulator subsystem

Pull request #3805 adds V3KN account, network, hashing, and storage state to EmuEnv. The Vita-style interface exposes Online Storage from supported title contexts and shows local and cloud metadata side by side. Upload and download enter explicit confirmation and copying states, with percentage and remaining-time feedback. Delete and saved-data auto-upload controls share the authenticated connection rather than embedding requests directly in individual UI widgets.
Transfer state separates network work from presentation

Progress values, remaining duration, discovered savedata information, and operation mode live in the storage subsystem while GUI code renders them. Account dialogs manage sign-in and connection errors, and network utilities centralize transport behavior. The destination is overwritten only after the user sees source and target details. Titles outside the expected Vita ID shape do not expose a cloud action, limiting accidental use on non-game entries.
Failure testing must protect both copies

Upload and download empty saves, large saves, nested files, Unicode names, and rapid successive changes. Interrupt DNS, authentication, connection, and process execution at every phase, then confirm the local directory and last valid remote object remain recoverable. Test clock differences, equal timestamps with different hashes, two machines editing the same title, cancellation near completion, token expiration, and auto-upload on exit. Server responses and extracted paths require validation before any destination replacement.
Cloud save convenience is only trustworthy when the interface exposes the conflict and the transfer code preserves a last known-good copy on either side.
